info.title: Interf Local Service API
info.summary: Human-readable contract for the Interf local service.
info.description: This OpenAPI document describes the local Runtime API used by the CLI, MCP, and authorized clients.

Revoke the Interf account session held by this device, then clear the exact captured local session. A newer login survives the revoke wait; an account deletion that is already committing explicitly retains the session until deletion finishes; and an unconfirmed account revoke is reported as pending with the reason.
Set or clear the Interf account app URL used by Studio, CLI, and the local service. This stores an Interf-owned URL, never a vendor URL.

post.description: Cancel one active portable Run through its Runtime-owned cancellation authority.

Pause one unsettled portable Run. The in-flight Attempt is abandoned and no Worker can claim, advance, or settle the Run while it is paused. The response quotes what continuing costs: the remainder after the stages the receipts ledger already holds, or a FULL re-run at the Build Plan's existing cost stop when it holds none. Never a resume of the abandoned Attempt.

Continue one durable Run through its archived authority by starting a new Attempt at a new fence. Completed stages the receipts ledger holds are re-entered, never executed again, and the response names them: the quote is the remainder. Without a stage checkpoint this re-runs the whole Run at the Build Plan's existing cost stop. Either way it does not resume the abandoned Attempt. Retry may name from_stage to restore the exact Graph snapshot after that checkpointed completed stage before the new Attempt; omitted, the last checkpoint is used, and an uncheckpointed stage is refused with a typed error. On the local plane the request may name a different connected agent for the new Attempt, verified live exactly as Build admission verifies one; omitted, the Run continues on the agent its current Attempt holds. A managed Run executes the Interf-provided agent pinned by its Worker release and refuses a named agent. Its managed_recovery request must bind the published predecessor Attempt, fence, reservation and checkpoint; commercial admission reserves the fresh Attempt atomically after prior settlement and cleanup. A Graph handoff refuses a named agent on either plane because it runs the carrier it was admitted with.
